    "quote_a": "| C1 Bytes | The verifier reconstructs each signer's exact frame; both bind the same content and common metadata, the designated fingerprint in its slot. The receipt-anchor preimage `A_sig` over both frames and both signatures is unambiguous. | Nothing about meaning or truth. Payload identity is not frame equality. |",
    "loc_b": "ENCODING-V1.md:308-310",
    "quote_b": "F_kms = 11 'tessera-v1/attest' 0001 u32(L_kms) '{\"common\":' JCS(C) ',\"signer\":{\"key_fp\":' JCS(fp_kms) '}}'\nF_gpg = 11 'tessera-v1/attest' 0001 u32(L_gpg) '{\"common\":' JCS(C) ',\"signer\":{\"key_fp\":' JCS(fp_gpg) '}}'",
    "kind": "term",
    "explanation": "C1 says both frames bind the same content and common metadata, but ENCODING-V1 shows the frames differ in length and signer member, not just fingerprint; payload identity is not frame equality.",
    "confidence": "medium"
  },
  {
    "loc_a": "phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:144",
    "quote_a": "| C4 Authority | DNSSEC (owner name D, evaluated at the snapshot's own anchored time) and the anchored git key assertion (full commit→tree→blob path) authenticated K for D, with the issuance window, at their evidence times. **Chain-order pre-commitment** (OWNER DECISION 2026-10-14, BROADEN; `docs/reviews/spec-sufficiency/` F01): the git assertion's selected anchor height plus 5 is lower than the receipt's selected anchor height, so the window was confirmed at k = 6 in the chain before the receipt was anchored. The verifier fixes the required set. | Revocation not evaluated. Not public publication of the commit. Neither channel commits to any receipt (CODEX-REVIEW 3). Pre-commitment is chain order, not UTC (A2.1); DNSSEC evidence establishes no publication before issue. |",
    "loc_b": "V1-PROFILE.md:710-713",
    "quote_b": "- **chain-order pre-commitment: h_git + 5 < h_receipt**, else `INVALID / GIT_NOT_PRECOMMITTED` (A9 C4 as revised 2026-10-14, OWNER DECISION, BROADEN);",
    "kind": "verdict",
    "explanation": "C4 says git assertion's selected anchor height plus 5 is lower than receipt's selected anchor height; V1-PROFILE says h_git + 5 < h_receipt else INVALID. This matches, but note the term 'selected anchor height' vs 'h_git' and 'h_receipt'.",
    "confidence": "high"
  },
  {
    "loc_a": "phase0-prereg-amendment-9.md:145",
    "quote_a": "| C5 Time | The frames **and their exact signatures** existed no later than T, the verified attestation at the lowest block height in the presented OTS proof (both T and its confirmations come from that attestation; OWNER DECISION 2026-10-14, F03: header times are not monotone, so \"earliest\" means chain order); the three-conjunct predicate holds at k = 6. | Presentation-sensitive T. No lower bound, no priority. Header times are chain-time proxies. Reorganization deeper than k is a residual. |",
    "loc_b": "V1-PROFILE.md:770-775",
    "quote_b": "- T is the time of the verified attestation at the **lowest block height** in the presented OTS proof; both T and\n  its confirmations come from that attestation. It is presentation-sensitive: a different presentation of the same\n  receipt can select a different T. [A9 C5 as revised 2026-10-14; DD:56, 98-99; OWNER 2026-10-14, G03] *Dated\n  correction 2026-10-14: this bullet previously read \"T is the time of the earliest verified attestation\", A9's\n  earlier wording. \"Earliest\" means chain order, not least nTime: header times are not monotone, and the two\n  selection rules can give different verdicts on the same proof.*",
    "kind": "term",
    "explanation": "C5 says 'lowest block height' and 'earliest' means chain order; V1-PROFILE clarifies that 'earliest' was earlier wording and now uses 'lowest block height'. This is a clarification, not a contradiction.",
    "confidence": "medium"
  },
  {
    "loc_a": "phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:150",
    "quote_a": "- **Trust configuration** (ships with the verifier, never from the bundle): root KSK-2017 and KSK-2024 with separate\n  publication, signing and reliance periods; the repository key; a signed, versioned set of pinned mainnet header hashes.\n  A bundle header outside the pins gives `UNVERIFIABLE / HEADERS_NOT_COVERED`. The trust configuration's KSK\n  periods are as known at release; snapshots after an unlisted rollover are `UNVERIFIABLE`.",
    "loc_b": "V1-PROFILE.md:532-534",
    "quote_b": "- **Header pins.** A bundle header at a height with no pin gives `UNVERIFIABLE / HEADERS_NOT_COVERED`. A **selected**\n  anchor (section 7.1) beyond the newest pin is `UNVERIFIABLE`; an unselected attestation without its headers\n  supplies no fact and is not a failure. [A9:150; A9 C6 as revised 2026-10-14; OWNER 2026-10-14, G05]",
    "kind": "verdict",
    "explanation": "Both agree on UNVERIFIABLE / HEADERS_NOT_COVERED for a header outside pins, but V1-PROFILE adds nuance about selected anchor beyond newest pin.",
    "confidence": "high"
  },
  {
    "loc_a": "phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:291-292",
    "quote_a": "- **Receipt anchor.** OTS stamps `SHA256(A_sig)`, tag `tessera-v1/receipt-anchor-sig`, which commits to both frames\n  and their exact detached signatures in manifest slot order (ENCODING-V1 §5, D-8, D-14). The verifier verifies the\n  committed signature bytes only. The frame-only layout is withdrawn, with no fallback.",
    "loc_b": "ENCODING-V1.md:375-378",
    "quote_b": "A_sig = header(\"tessera-v1/receipt-anchor-sig\") ‖ u8 0x02\n        ‖ u32 len(F_kms) ‖ F_kms ‖ u32 len(S_kms) ‖ S_kms\n        ‖ u32 len(F_gpg) ‖ F_gpg ‖ u32 len(S_gpg) ‖ S_gpg\nanchor digest = SHA256(A_sig), the value OpenTimestamps stamps",
    "kind": "term",
    "explanation": "Both describe the same receipt anchor construction, committing to frames and exact signatures.",
    "confidence": "high"
  },
  {
    "loc_a": "phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:297-298",
    "quote_a": "- **Git stamp target (D-16).** The git channel's OTS stamp targets the **signed commit's object id**, never a tree,\n  blob or unsigned commit. The verifier recomputes the id, verifies `gpgsig`, follows commit→tree→blob, and checks\n  the stamped id. SHA-1 linkage remains a stated residual. The git evidence names its object format, and V1\n  accepts only `sha1`: the key-assertion repository stays in SHA-1 format at a host that supports it, whatever\n  git's default becomes (the author, 2026-10-13: Git 3 moves to SHA-256 in 2027; GitHub does not support it).\n  The pre-freeze bundle schema (V1-PROFILE §2.1, G-26) defines the git-evidence member `object_format` as the string\n  `\"sha1\"`. It is an evidence descriptor, not a new signed-frame or key-publication field. A missing descriptor gives\n  `UNVERIFIABLE / GIT_OBJECT_FORMAT_MISSING`; an unsupported value gives `UNVERIFIABLE / GIT_OBJECT_FORMAT`. The\n  verifier recomputes the SHA-1 object ids from the raw commit/tree/blob bytes, so this descriptor cannot override\n  their interpretation. For V1 the stamped message is exactly 40 lowercase ASCII hex digits naming the signed commit\n  id followed by one LF byte. The schema/check specification and conformance cases are fixed before the 30 Oct\n  profile freeze; no P8 frame or key-publication vector changes are required.",
    "loc_b": "V1-PROFILE.md:648-655",
    "quote_b": "The OTS stamp targets the signed commit's object id, never a tree, blob or unsigned commit. [A9:282-284; ENC\n§7.2:685-691] The verifier does four things:\n\n1. Recomputes the commit id from the presented raw commit object.\n2. Verifies `gpgsig` over the object without that header, under the pinned repository key.\n3. Follows commit, then tree, then blob, down the fixed path below.\n4. Checks that the stamped bytes name that id.",
    "kind": "term",
    "explanation": "Both describe the same git stamp target and verification steps.",
    "confidence": "high"
  },
  {
    "loc_a": "phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:309-310",
    "quote_a": "- **Root-KSK rule.** The root DNSKEY set is valid at the snapshot's anchored time **if some trusted KSK whose reliance\n  period contains that time validates it**. Each KSK entry records signing-start, signing-end and a sourced reliance\n  lifetime L, with the reliance interval [signing-start, signing-end + L]. L is the registered acceptance-policy\n  value derived from the cited root DNSKEY RRSIG validity evidence; a largest observed lifetime is labelled observed,\n  not asserted to be a proven global maximum. A candidate must also satisfy cryptographic validation and the selected\n  RRSIG's inception/expiration checks at the snapshot's own verified anchored time. This extension permits authentic\n  pre-retirement evidence anchored later; it does not establish that signing occurred before retirement. A thief of\n  a retired KSK can manufacture eligible root evidence during the extension. Exposure is bounded by the reliance\n  endpoint in snapshot chain time, not by a finite UTC duration under A2.1. Historical authority-key safety and the\n  continuing anchor/history assumptions remain necessary and are not evaluated by V1. **AUTHOR ADOPTED, 2026-10-13**\n  (`docs/reviews/v1-profile/` F2; kind CORRECT: the withdrawn cutoff claimed a protection DNSSEC itself does not\n  supply, since resolvers accept a retired KSK's signatures until they expire). The author: *\"I'd argue that the\n  'narrowing of protection' wasn't a real narrowing, it was us admitting the real level of protection given the\n  constraints of the project.\"* The rule is existential and order-independent: a candidate that fails is\n  informational, and the result is computed once, after every eligible key has been tried (F1). A trusted KSK that\n  is published but did not sign is informational, never a failure. The trust configuration records signing and\n  reliance periods separately from publication and revocation dates.",
    "loc_b": "V1-PROFILE.md:415-424",
    "quote_b": "- **Root rule.** The root DNSKEY set is valid at the snapshot's anchored time if some trusted KSK whose **reliance\n  period** contains that time validates it. Each KSK entry records signing-start, signing-end and a sourced reliance lifetime L; the reliance\n  interval is [signing-start, signing-end + L]. L is an acceptance-policy value from cited RRSIG validity evidence,\n  labelled observed, not a proven global maximum. The extension admits authentic pre-retirement evidence anchored\n  later and does not prove signing before retirement: a thief of a retired KSK can manufacture eligible evidence\n  during it (A9.5; AUTHOR ADOPTED 2026-10-13, kind CORRECT). *Dated correction 2026-10-13: the earlier wording\n  (\"maximum validity … it made\"; \"usable for that long and no longer\") overclaimed provenance and is withdrawn.* The rule is existential and\n  order-independent: a candidate that fails is informational, and the result is computed once, after every eligible\n  key has been tried. A trusted KSK that is published but did not sign is informational, never a failure.\n  [A9.5, A9:296-303, OWNER DECISION 2026-10-13 after `docs/reviews/v1-profile/` F1, F2]",
    "kind": "term",
    "explanation": "Both describe the same root-KSK rule with reliance periods.",
    "confidence": "high"
  },
  {
    "loc_a": "phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:333-334",
    "quote_a": "- **Trust configuration is append-only** (OWNER DECISION 2026-10-13). Trust configuration entries are append-only: KSKs, header\n  pins and repository keys are never removed, and finalized period endpoints never change. Repository trust entries\n  name D, the key and an inclusive signing interval; the git assertion passes this trust check if some configured\n  entry for D verifies gpgsig and its interval contains the signed commit's own verified anchored time. Repository\n  entries have no KSK-style reliance extension. Unknown material cannot establish this required check. Append-only\n  extensions preserve previously usable trust witnesses; newly covered evidence can improve an earlier UNVERIFIABLE\n  result. Exact stable-field identity remains the contract for identical declared inputs. Closing an open period must\n  not retrospectively exclude evidence previously accepted under that entry; the pre-freeze configuration records the\n  endpoint/update convention explicitly. **Rollover control:** a snapshot taken while one trusted KSK is published but not signing must pass\n  (SPIKE-REPORT, KSK-2024 re-capture; without it every receipt from 2026-10-11 would be falsely rejected).",
    "loc_b": "V1-PROFILE.md:529-531",
    "quote_b": "They do **not** preserve every verdict: appending pins can make an earlier\n  attestation qualify and change T. A9.4's contract is exact output for identical declared inputs (the config is one);\n  no monotonic-verdict promise is made.",
    "kind": "verdict",
    "explanation": "A9 says append-only preserves previously usable trust witnesses; V1-PROFILE says appending pins can change T and verdict, not preserving every verdict. This is a clarification, not a contradiction.",
    "confidence": "medium"
  },
  {
    "loc_a": "phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:419-420",
    "quote_a": "- **Verifier rule (C4).** A receipt is `INVALID / ISSUANCE_WINDOW` unless the declared issue time is not earlier\n  than not-before and the verified chain-time T is not later than not-after, with T as registered and no margin.\n  T itself is not compared with not-before.",
    "loc_b": "V1-PROFILE.md:638-640",
    "quote_b": "- A receipt is `INVALID / ISSUANCE_WINDOW` unless `issuance-not-before` ≤ declared issue time and T ≤\n  `issuance-not-after`. Both bounds are inclusive. T is compared as registered, with no margin. T is not compared\n  with not-before. [A9:338-340; ENC §7.1:636-643, 662-663]",
    "kind": "verdict",
    "explanation": "Both describe the same issuance window rule with same verdict.",
    "confidence": "high"
  },
  {
    "loc_a": "phase-0-prereg-amendment-9.md:519-524",
    "quote_a": "prereg §4.3 and A1 P8 reject a number not exactly representable as an IEEE 754 double. That rule does not compose\nwith RFC 8785: it accepts inputs whose canonical form it then rejects (ENCODING-V1 §1.2). For `tessera-v1-strict`\nit is replaced by: **accept a number exactly when RFC 8785's canonical serialization preserves its value; reject\notherwise.** Proof: `formal/p8/PROOF.md` Lemma 3. Vectors: `formal/p8/vectors/`.",
    "loc_b": "V1-PROFILE.md:1010-1013",
    "quote_b": "Accept a number exactly when RFC 8785's canonical serialization preserves its value. Reject otherwise. The three\nconditions (not negative zero, finite after round-half-even, exact decimal value of `ES(d)` equals the literal) and\nthe accepted and rejected examples are in ENC §1.2. [A9:438-443; ENC §1.2:118-148; ENC D-1:752-755] Proof:\n`formal/p8/PROOF.md` Lemma 3. Vectors: `formal/p8/vectors/`.",
    "kind": "term",
    "explanation": "Both describe the same number rule replacement for V1.",
    "confidence": "high"
  }
]
